FULL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Can CAM-UV discover causal relationships in data with unobserved common causes?" (design-only deliverable; no experiment has been run and no results are reported)

====================================================================
1. RATIONALE AND RESEARCH QUESTION
====================================================================
Research question: Does CAM-UV (Causal Additive Model with Unobserved Variables; Maeda & Shimizu, LiNGAM-family lineage) recover (i) causal structure among observed variables and (ii) the presence of unobserved common causes, and does it do so better than methods that assume causal sufficiency?

Rationale: Classical LiNGAM-family methods identify causal structure from non-Gaussianity but assume no latent confounders. CAM-UV extends this to nonlinear additive models and outputs both an observed-variable causal matrix and a pairwise indicator of inferred latent common causes. A controlled synthetic study is the appropriate test because ground-truth latent structure is unobservable in real data; only simulation makes the pair-level latent target directly scoreable.

Primary outcome (stated as an assumption, per A4): the pair-level latent-confounder detection performance (precision/recall/F1 of the set of observed-variable pairs flagged as sharing an unobserved common cause, against the generator's latent pair set). Secondary outcome: directed-edge structure metrics among observed variables. This prioritization is an assumption of the design, not an established fact.

====================================================================
2. DATA-GENERATING MODEL (SEM SPECIFICATION)
====================================================================
2.1 Graph generation
- Observed DAG over p variables drawn once per (condition, seed) from a random-DAG generator (Erdős–Rényi orientation of a fixed variable ordering; expected edge density ≈ 1.0–1.5 edges/node — a convention, tuned if degenerate).
- Latent confounders: m latent nodes L_k (m = ⌈p/5⌉, a convention), each assigned ≥2 observed children chosen from the DAG's variables; latent nodes do not cause each other (single-layer latent structure, assumption A3).

2.2 Structural equations
For each observed variable j:
  X_j = Σ_{i ∈ pa_obs(j)} f_ij(X_i) + Σ_{k ∈ pa_lat(j)} g_kj(L_k) + e_j
- Linear condition: f_ij(x) = b_ij · x, |b_ij| ∈ [0.5, 1.5] (convention).
- Nonlinear condition: f_ij drawn from a fixed family {a·x, a·tanh(x), a·sin(x), a·x + c·x², a·x + c·x³} with coefficients scaled so the function's effect size over the observed input range matches the linear condition's target R² contribution (standardized inputs; coefficients chosen to avoid range blow-up). A "near-linear" difficulty setting uses the nonlinear family with the nonlinear component scaled to ~10% of the linear component (see §3, difficulty conditions).
- Latent influence g_kj: linear loading β_kj · L_k with |β_kj| set per confounder-strength condition (§3); the latent contribution is targeted to account for a specified share of the child's variance (see §3 for the operationalization).
- Latent distribution: L_k drawn i.i.d. non-Gaussian (mixture of two shifted Laplace distributions, giving an asymmetric, heavy-tailed non-Gaussian source) — consistent with the non-Gaussianity the method family relies on.

2.3 Noise families
- Non-Gaussian (default): e_j ~ Laplace(0, 1), independently across variables (i.i.d., independent of parents and latents).
- Gaussian (stress-test condition): e_j ~ N(0, 1).
All variables standardized (zero mean, unit variance) before handing to methods, using statistics computed from the generated sample (identical preprocessing for all methods).

2.4 Ground truth for scoring
- Observed edge set E* = directed edges in pa_obs.
- Latent pair set P* = unordered pairs {i, j} sharing at least one common latent parent.
- Edge weights are thresholded at generation time so that "an edge exists" is unambiguous (weights are bounded away from zero by construction, |b| ≥ 0.5).

====================================================================
3. CONDITIONS (FACTORIAL STRUCTURE)
====================================================================
Core factorial (all runs at p = 10, non-Gaussian noise, 50 seeds/cell):
  F1 Functional form: {linear, nonlinear} (2)
  F2 Latent confounding: {none, weak, strong} (3)
  F3 Sample size n: {200, 500, 1000, 2000} (4)
  → 24 core cells.

Operationalization of F2: "none" = no latent nodes; "weak" = latent contribution explains ~10% of each affected child's variance; "strong" = ~40% (both shares are conventions to be tuned, per U5, not facts; a small pilot grid over shares is part of the design if execution were ever in scope).

Targeted extension cells (smaller seed count, e.g., 20 seeds/cell, to keep the design bounded):
  E1 Dimension: repeat the core grid at p = 5 (24 cells) to test small-dimension behavior.
  E2 Gaussian-noise stress test: repeat the nonlinear × latent cells at n = 1000 under Gaussian noise (6 cells) — hypothesis: identifiability of latent pairs degrades; informative, not a failure of the design.
  E3 Near-linear difficulty condition: nonlinear family with ~10% nonlinear component, at {no-latent, weak, strong} × n = 1000 (3 cells). Per the researcher's instruction, U3 is treated as a planned difficulty condition that is informative for the comparison, not a risk to be avoided.

Sanity condition (embedded in the core grid): linear × no-latent × non-Gaussian — the regime where DirectLiNGAM is expected to succeed; the design requires that CAM-UV's observed-structure performance there not be materially worse than DirectLiNGAM's (pre-registered tolerance: F1 within ~0.1 of the baseline — a convention, tunable).

====================================================================
4. METHODS UNDER COMPARISON
====================================================================
  M1 CAM-UV (primary treatment). Specification: pairwise independence/overfitting-adjusted independence measures on residuals of candidate parent sets; outputs observed causal matrix + latent-pair indicator matrix. Hyperparameters are NOT asserted as facts (U1): the design specifies a sensitivity grid — independence threshold α ∈ {0.01, 0.005, 0.001} (convention), max number of parents ∈ {2, 3}, number of fake/overfitting-control variables ∈ {p, 2p} — with all results reported both at a pre-registered default (the implementation's documented default, to be confirmed from source at implementation time) and across the grid.
  M2 DirectLiNGAM (sufficiency-assuming baseline). Outputs an observed causal matrix only; its latent-pair prediction is the empty set by construction (so its latent recall is 0 by definition — the latent comparison is therefore primarily CAM-UV vs. RCD, with DirectLiNGAM quantifying what is lost by assuming sufficiency).
  M3 RCD (Ranking-based causal discovery; Maeda & Shimizu) — second latent-handling comparator, included as method specification only (no execution required); it also outputs observed structure plus latent-pair information, giving the primary outcome a non-trivial comparator.

All three methods receive identical input matrices per (condition, seed); no method-specific preprocessing beyond the shared standardization.

====================================================================
5. CONTROLS
====================================================================
  C1 Paired design: the same (condition, seed) datasets are fed to all three methods; comparisons are paired across seeds.
  C2 Fixed generation procedure: one generator implementation, fixed random-seed stream per cell; the DAG, latents, coefficients, and noise draws are all seeded.
  C3 Generator self-checks (to be run at implementation time, not now): (a) verify that confounded pairs are statistically dependent in generated samples (marginal dependence check), (b) verify that non-confounded non-adjacent pairs are approximately independent in the linear no-latent condition, (c) verify standardized variances. These are sanity checks on the harness, not results.
  C4 Identical preprocessing across methods (§2.3).
  C5 Hyperparameter sensitivity is reported rather than cherry-picked (§4); the default-configuration headline numbers are pre-registered before the grid is examined (a design commitment).
  C6 Runtime per fit is recorded for every run to make compute cost transparent (§9).

====================================================================
6. ANALYSIS PLAN
====================================================================
6.1 Metrics
  Primary (pair-level latent detection): precision, recall, F1 over the predicted latent-pair set vs. P*.
  Secondary (observed structure): directed-edge precision, recall, F1, and SHD vs. E*. For latent-aware methods, the latent-pair output is excluded from the observed-edge score (a pair flagged as confounded is not counted as a directed-edge error), matching each method's own output semantics.
  Descriptive: causal-ordering agreement (optional tertiary metric), runtime.

6.2 Statistical treatment
  - Per cell: mean ± 95% CI over seeds (bootstrap or t-interval, stated at analysis time).
  - Paired method comparisons within each cell: permutation test on seed-paired differences (e.g., CAM-UV − DirectLiNGAM F1), with Holm correction across the reported cell family.
  - Factor effects: mixed-effects / decomposition of metric variance over F1–F3 with seed as random effect; focus on the form × latent interaction (hypothesis: CAM-UV's advantage grows with confounder presence and strength).
  - Sensitivity analysis: metric spread across the hyperparameter grid per cell, reported alongside headline numbers.

====================================================================
7. EXPECTED OUTCOMES — HYPOTHESES (explicitly hypotheses, not findings)
====================================================================
  H1: In the linear × strong-latent regime, CAM-UV and RCD achieve materially higher latent-pair F1 than DirectLiNGAM (whose recall is 0 by construction).
  H2: In the nonlinear × latent regimes, CAM-UV's latent-pair F1 exceeds RCD's (its nonlinearity handling is the claimed advantage) — this is the design's central hypothesis and may fail; either outcome is informative.
  H3: In the sanity condition (linear, no latent), CAM-UV's observed-structure F1 is within the pre-registered tolerance of DirectLiNGAM's.
  H4: Latent-pair F1 for CAM-UV increases with n across the tested range, plateauing by n ≈ 1000 (conventional expectation; A1 is exactly what the n-factor tests).
  H5: Under Gaussian noise (E2), latent detection degrades for all latent-aware methods, consistent with the non-Gaussianity assumption (A2).
  H6: In the near-linear difficulty condition (E3), the CAM-UV/RCD advantage over DirectLiNGAM shrinks toward zero — quantifying where the latent-handling benefit disappears.
No result is claimed; these are the predictions the design is built to discriminate.

====================================================================
8. LIMITATIONS
====================================================================
  L1: Synthetic-only validity; real-data generalization is not tested (no credible ground-truth latent data is assumed available).
  L2: Single-layer, additive latent structure (A3); CAM-UV's behavior under latent-to-latent causation or interaction-type confounding is out of scope.
  L3: Pair-level latent scoring treats a shared-confounder relation as binary; graded confounder strength is only manipulated, not scored continuously.
  L4: Metric semantics differ across methods (DirectLiNGAM cannot output latent pairs), so the primary outcome is a two-way comparison in practice.
  L5: Hyperparameter sensitivity may dominate small-sample cells; headline conclusions are therefore tied to the pre-registered default configuration.

====================================================================
9. FEASIBILITY (honest statement)
====================================================================
  - A0 (implementation availability): the design specifies the `lingam` Python package's CAM-UV and RCD implementations and DirectLiNGAM as the intended implementation choice, with a documented fallback of re-implementing CAM-UV from the original paper if the package is unavailable. Availability must be confirmed at implementation time; this design does not assert it as fact.
  - A5 (compute): CPU-only is assumed sufficient at p ≤ 10, n ≤ 2000; kernel-based independence measures are the main cost driver, and runtime is recorded per fit (C6) so the assumption is checkable. Rough per-fit runtime is unknown (uncertainty) and budgeted conservatively in the design (order of seconds-to-minutes per fit; a convention, not a measurement).
  - U4 (Python 3.14 compatibility): this matters only insofar as the design must name a runnable implementation choice; the design therefore specifies pinning a supported Python version (e.g., 3.11/3.12 venv) for the implementation environment. Execution itself is out of scope for this task.
  - U1/U5 (hyperparameters and effect strengths): no defaults or strength ranges are asserted as facts; all such values above are labeled conventions inside pre-specified sensitivity/tuning grids.
  - Current workspace reality: /workspace contains only task.json (which itself notes "Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required"); track.md is not materialized on disk; numpy/scipy are not installed and network is disabled — consistent with a written design being the sole deliverable.

====================================================================
10. FIXED REQUIREMENTS VS. ASSUMPTIONS (separated)
====================================================================
Fixed by the task: design-only; no claim that an experiment was run; no simulated results; no repositories/datasets/compute assumed.
Assumptions (this design's own commitments, revisable): A0 implementation obtainable; A1 sample-size adequacy (tested by H4, not presumed); A2 non-Gaussian noise needed for latent identifiability (tested by E2/H5); A3 single-layer additive latents; A4 pair-level latent indicator as primary outcome; A5 CPU sufficiency (checked via C6).
Uncertainties carried forward: U1 hyperparameter defaults (handled by §4 grids + pre-registered default); U2 exact output format of the implementation (confirmed from source at implementation time); U3 handled as planned difficulty condition E3; U4 handled as a pinned-environment implementation choice; U5 effect-strength ranges as tuned conventions.

Deliverable form: a single written design document containing §1–§10 above, with the SEM specification (§2) and metric definitions (§6) precise enough that an implementer could execute it without further design decisions.
